definition: The N1 component is an event-related brain response used to examine very early stages of attention during information processing. In this source, differences in N1 amplitude are interpreted as showing changes in early attentional control and the speed of early attention processing under emotional interference.

reasons: The definition states that the “N1 component is an event-related brain response.” The provided packet does not explicitly define N1 as an event-related brain response (it only describes using ERP experiments and reports effects of N1 component amplitude).

The definition claims that “differences in N1 amplitude are interpreted as showing changes in early attentional control and the speed of early attention processing under emotional interference.” While the packet reports that smaller N1 amplitude in proficient bilinguals is associated with the influence existing in the “early attention stage” and says it “improve[s] … attentional control and speed up attention processing,” the packet does not explicitly frame this as an interpretation of “differences in N1 amplitude” in those specific terms.
